To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glucosepane levels in skin correlate with retinopathy and are independent of glycemic control, and that the DCCT cohort provides a unique opportunity to study the relationship of AGEs with diabetic complications and their progression.

the DCCT is a rich source of human tissue and data that can be used to understand the pathophysiology of diabetes and its complications, and that we need to know much more about glucosepane and other AGEs.

(i) Glucosepane, the most abundant protein cross-link in diabetic tissues, is a major determinant of diabetic complications and (ii) the glucose/fructose-lactose/lysine/glucose-pane axis is the strongest marker of diabetic retinopathy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of sensitive, specific and robust assays for AGEs in order to understand the biology of these adducts in diabetes and aging, and to use these markers to develop and test novel therapies for diabetic complications.
the development and application of new analytical tools for quantitating AGEs in biological fluids and tissues and the use of these methods to study the pathogenesis of diabetic complications.
the identification and quantitation of novel AGEs and the elucidation of the biological roles of AGEs in diabetes and its complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucosepane is a poorly understood advanced-glycation end-product of growing importance for diabetic and other chronic metabolic diseases of the aging process.
the AGE glucosepane is a poorly understood advanced glycated end product of growing clinical importance for diabetes and diabetic complications.
the glucosepane hypothesis is still a hypothesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AGE axis, and especially the glucosepane axis, is a robust marker for diabetic microvascular disease, and that the DCCT has been a rich source for the study of AGEs in diabetes.
the AGEs are a heterogeneous family of compounds with different biological activities and that the most abundant and most biologically important AGEs are not yet known.
AGE formation is a major complication of diabetes, but that the most prevalent AGEs are poorly understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that

glucosepane is the predominant protein-bound AGE of the extracellular space and is associated with the progression of microvascular complications, especially retinopathies, in type 1 diabetes, in spite of the adjustment for average glycemia and other AGEs.

the DCCT has been a unique resource for studying AGEs, and the data obtained to date have been a valuable resource for the field of diabetes research and care, and for the development of novel therapeutic approaches.
the DCCT is a rich resource of human samples for studies on the role of AGEs in diabetic complications, and the DCCT is an ideal resource for studies on the pathophysiology of diabetic retinopathy.
